Shape-rankkmed: Ranked K-medoids on Kendall's 2D shape space

Source: R/shape_rankkmed.R
shape_rankkmed.Rd

Shape-rankkmed: Ranked K-medoids on Kendall's 2D shape space

Usage

shape_rankkmed(
  Z,
  K,
  distance = c("rho", "dF"),
  m = 5L,
  max_iter = 30L,
  initial = NULL
)

Arguments

Z

Complex pre-shape matrix of size (k-1) x n, a numeric distance matrix of size n x n, or a real landmark array of dimension k x m x n with m = 2 or 3 (distances from shape_distance).

K

Number of clusters (>= 2).

distance

Character. One of "rho" (default), "dF".

m

Neighbourhood size for cluster formation (default 5; Zadegan et al. (2013) recommend 5-15).

max_iter

Integer. Maximum number of iterations (default 30). The loop stops earlier at a fixed point (medoids unchanged and no relocation), from which further iterations cannot move.

initial

Optional vector of length K giving initial medoid indices (1-based).

Value

A list with components:

cluster

Integer vector of length n, values in 1:K.

medoids

Integer vector of length K.

objective

Sum of distances of each object to its medoid.

n_iter

Number of iterations performed.

distance

Distance name used.

Details

With the same distance matrix, initial medoids and random-number stream, the partition equals that of kmed::rankkmed run with iterate = max_iter.

References

Zadegan, S. M. R., Mirzaie, M. and Sadoughi, F. (2013). Ranked k-medoids: a fast and accurate rank-based partitioning algorithm for clustering large datasets. Knowledge-Based Systems, 39, 133–143. doi:10.1016/j.knosys.2012.10.012

Examples

set.seed(1)
k <- 4; n <- 30
X <- array(rnorm(k * 2 * n), dim = c(k, 2, n))
Z <- landmarks_to_preshape(X)
fit <- shape_rankkmed(Z, K = 3, m = 5)
table(fit$cluster)
#> 
#>  1  2  3 
#> 10  8 12
